title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: US markets closed at record highs on 6 October, NBC News reports, but the gains are narrow: BeInCrypto, citing Axios, reports that a Goldman Sachs index that leaves out companies it counts as AI enablers rose 6.7% in six months against 18.3% for the S&P 500, where Goldman counts about 45% as AI enablers. Fact: research firm Dell'Oro says data centre spending rose 92% in the second quarter, and Reuters reports that US software shares hit their highest since November 2025 as fears of AI wrecking their business faded.

Fact: more of the building is paid with borrowed money. The Financial Times reports, citing unnamed sources, that SpaceX is seeking about $40 billion in loans and bonds for Nvidia chips, and the Wall Street Journal reports that the cloud company Lambda is raising up to $4 billion on an order book that appears to rest largely on one customer, Anthropic. Fact: Bloomberg reports that investor Ray Dalio called AI a "classic bubble" and said "we're close" to the bursting point, pointing to heavy borrowing and rising interest rates. Fact: Heatmap News counts at least $260 billion of US data centre projects cancelled this year after local opposition, a figure not independently confirmed.

Our view: the rally rests on a small group of AI companies, and more of their building now runs on debt while borrowing costs rise. The real test is on the ground: whether the data centres get power, local approval and paying customers.

What to watch and follow. 1. Local votes on data centres, after San Francisco and Raleigh paused approvals; each pause delays the spending the market expects. 2. AI debt deals such as SpaceX's; a failed or repriced deal would show lenders getting nervous. 3. Job cuts that name AI, at FICO, HSBC and Norway's DNB; they show where companies expect savings, while studies so far find little effect on pay or hiring. 4. Mistral's promised open model weights in about three weeks; they decide whether its performance claims can be tested.
Unknowns. The SpaceX and DeepSeek fundraising figures come from unnamed sources and could change, and Heatmap's cancellation count has not been checked by others.
